Split a GPU table into one GPU table per group (dplyr backend method)

Source: R/fallback.R
group_split.tbl_gpu.Rd

Native: dplyr::group_split() on a tbl_gpu groups by ... (or uses the existing groups), computes the group row indices on the GPU (compute_group_data(): sorted keys, NA last, .drop = FALSE and preserved empty groups), gathers the rows into group order and cuts the table at the group sizes (gpu_split_rows()). The chunks are tbl_gpu tables, as dplyr's chunks have the class of the ungrouped input, and the list_of ptype is a 0-row tbl_gpu. A table left with no columns (every column dropped by .keep = FALSE) is the one case that still goes through the CPU fallback.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
group_split(.tbl, ..., .keep = TRUE, keep = lifecycle::deprecated())

Arguments

.tbl

A tbl.

...

If .tbl is an ungrouped data frame, a grouping specification, forwarded to group_by().

.keep

Should the grouping columns be kept?

keep

Defunct, use .keep.

Value

A vctrs::list_of() of tbl_gpu tables.
